identity.title: Morse index stability for critical points to conformally invariant Lagrangians

findings.title: Lemma V.1 substitutes a limiting length for a nonzero finite-stage logarithmic error
findings.status: Confirmed from the bound source text, an analytic counterexample, and independent symbolic calculations; confirmed against actual cited source-page images in [internal task].
findings.source_location: PDF/printed p.36, Lemma V.1, (V.1)-(V.3); proof pp.37-38; Theorem I.2 p.6 is a separate global claim.
findings.quantified_claim: Uniform C>0 and beta in (0,2), independent of k, bound r^2|grad u_k|^2 by boundary-decay factors times E(A(2eta,delta_k)) plus C*Lambda^2/log^2(eta^2/delta_k).
all_hypotheses_checked: Target S1 is a closed smooth submanifold; two-form is zero.
u_k=exp(i log(r)/k^2) is smooth and harmonic on every punctured annulus, including A(eta,delta_k) and A(2eta,delta_k).
Every doubling-annulus energy is 2*pi*log(2)/k^4, uniformly tending to zero.
Averaged radial length is (k+2*log(eta))/k^2 for large k, so the iterated limiting Lambda is exactly zero.
The printed lemma is explicitly local on A(eta,delta_k); it states no whole-disk criticality, actual-bubble-scale, or extra Hopf restriction.
findings.counterexample: At r_k=exp(-k/2), the left side is k^-4. The proposed right-side to left-side ratio is 4*pi*C*eta^-beta*exp(-beta*k/2)*(k+2*log(2eta)), which tends to zero for every fixed eta,C and beta>0.
findings.decisive_evidence: Exact harmonic-map residual is zero; exact annular energy and asymptotic ratio are recorded in independent_checks_stdout.txt. The analytic contradiction works for all sufficiently large k, not a finite numerical fit.
findings.impact: A false quantitative lemma in the collar proof of Theorem I.2; this is not a counterexample to the global closed-surface theorem.
findings.repair_boundary: Retain a finite-stage residual R_eta,k with lim_eta limsup_k log^2(eta^2/delta_k)*R_eta,k <= C*Lambda^2, or an eventual Lambda+epsilon bound. The example requires a nonzero residual even when Lambda=0. A full general corrected collar lemma is not proved here.
findings.alternative_readings: If extra full-disk criticality or global geometric conditions were intended, they must be supplied and justified in the statement. The local example has infinite energy across the missing origin and is explicitly not used against such stronger claims.
findings.source_image_confirmation: Actually inspected cited source pages; see source_view_evidence.
findings.historical_status: Confirmed from the bound source text, an analytic counterexample, and independent symbolic calculations; actual source-image confirmation remains pending.

findings.title: The weighted Wente estimate fails for boundary concentration because the weight tends to zero at r=1
findings.status: Confirmed by an explicit compactly supported Jacobian, exact Dirichlet solution, analytic scaling contradiction, and exact symbolic checks; confirmed against actual cited source-page images in [internal task].
findings.source_location: p.45, Lemma E.1, (E.1)-(E.3); p.49 Case 1; p.55 (F.7), with downstream Morrey estimates pp.54-56.
findings.quantified_claim: A universal C bounds integral r^2|grad phi|^2 by Ea times integral f(r)|grad b|^2, f=r^2 log^2(1+1/r) log(1+log(1/r)), for the zero-boundary Jacobian solution.
all_hypotheses_checked: psi=(1-|xi|^2)_+^4 has a C3 compact extension; phi0=partial_2 psi is C2 compact; b0=-Delta psi is C1 compact.
a0=xi_1 chi(|xi|^2), chi=1 for s<=1, (s-4)^2(2s+1)/27 for 1<s<4, 0 for s>=4, is C1 compact in the closed ball of radius2.
All inputs are W1,2; J(a0,b0)=partial_2 b0=-Delta phi0 without boundary distribution terms.
After scaling by epsilon around (1-3epsilon,0), all supports are strictly inside B1 and phi has zero boundary trace.
Dirichlet energies are invariant under the two-dimensional scaling.
findings.counterexample: The scaled phi and b supports satisfy 1-4epsilon<=r<=1-2epsilon. The left side is at least (1-4epsilon)^2 Ephi, while the claimed right side is <=32*C*Ea*Eb*epsilon. Choosing epsilon<min(1/10,9Ephi/(800*C*Ea*Eb)) gives a strict contradiction.
findings.decisive_evidence: Exact Ephi=384*pi/35, Eb=3072*pi/5, Ea=184*pi/35, Jacobian residual0, and limit f/(1-r)=log(2)^2 are retained. No finite-sample inference is used.
findings.impact: False core weighted analytic inequality and its explicit application at (F.7); the main index theorems themselves are not disproved.
findings.repair_boundary: The report proves the replacement weight r^2(1+log(1/r))^2 using the genuine dyadic gradient decomposition, Wente/off-diagonal harmonic bounds, geometric convolution, and tail Hardy inequality. It stays positive at r=1 and is o(r^alpha) for every 0<alpha<2; the following F.1/F.2 interface survives with changed constants. This is not full independent certification of all other proof steps.
findings.repair_verification_scope: Specific replacement inequality and its required weight properties; not independent acceptance of the whole paper.
findings.source_image_confirmation: Actually inspected cited source pages; see source_view_evidence.
findings.historical_status: Confirmed by an explicit compactly supported Jacobian, exact Dirichlet solution, analytic scaling contradiction, and exact symbolic checks; source-image confirmation pending.

findings.title: Nearest-point projection acceleration and a sphere projection-derivative sign are incorrect
findings.status: Confirmed by exact differentiation and the printed expressions; confirmed against actual cited source-page images in [internal task].
findings.source_location: p.10, paragraph before (II.1) and (II.1)-(II.2); p.11, first formula in (II.14), compared with the correct subsequent (II.15).
findings.quantified_claim: Off-target Dpi_{u+t phi}=P_{pi(u+t phi)} and acceleration D_wP_u phi for arbitrary ambient phi; dP sphere printed as a difference of tensor terms.
all_hypotheses_checked: Constant u=e1 into S1 is an allowed harmonic map on any closed surface.
Ambient variation phi=a e1+b e2 is smooth; for small t it stays within the tubular neighborhood before projection.
findings.counterexample: Actual second derivative is (-b^2,-2ab), but the printed acceleration is (-b^2,-ab); a=b=1 gives (-1,-2) versus (-1,-1). Dpi_z has the missing factor |z|^-1. Correct dP=-du tensor u-u tensor du; the printed antisymmetric expression also has the wrong contraction sign.
findings.decisive_evidence: Independent exact symbolic derivatives retained; derivative of a symmetric projection must be symmetric. The later (II.15) uses the correct negative contraction, rather than following from the incorrect printed tensor formula.
findings.impact: Local second-variation derivation identities; the final sphere Hessian and the later explicitly projected spectral operator are not refuted.
findings.repair_boundary: Use normal acceleration I(w,w), or choose the ambient variation tangent initially. At a critical point the acceleration difference pairs with the vanishing first variation. Correct the tensor sign. This recovers the relevant Hessian interface.

findings.title: Annular extension requires a homogeneous whole-plane class and a corrected outer cutoff
findings.status: Confirmed under the usual inhomogeneous W1,2 convention, with an exact local-input counterexample and an explicit repaired construction; confirmed against actual cited source-page images in [internal task].
findings.source_location: pp.42-43, Lemma C.1, (C.1)-(C.7), especially the outer cutoff displayed on p.43.
findings.quantified_claim: Every a in W1,2(B_R minus B_r), 0<2r<R, has an extension in inhomogeneous W1,2(C) with gradient energy controlled only by the annular gradient.
all_hypotheses_checked: a=1 is a function on the finite annulus, so it belongs to its inhomogeneous W1,2 space.
An extension must equal a on the original annulus.
findings.counterexample: The asserted bound forces the extension gradient to vanish. Its annular value forces the whole-plane constant1, which is not L2(C). The input constant is not claimed to belong to whole-plane W1,2.
findings.decisive_evidence: Zero-gradient connectedness and nonintegrability of the nonzero whole-plane constant give an exact contradiction. The displayed chi_R is identically1 on B_R and therefore cannot generally match the original outer boundary trace.
findings.impact: Function-space and construction errors in the extension lemma; gradient operations in the subsequent proof admit the corrected formulation.
findings.repair_boundary: Require Wloc1,2 and globally L2 gradient, with tilde a-a_R in W1,2(C). Use chi_{R/2} and the outer function breve a under the outer inversion. Scaled annular Poincare and conformal invariance prove the original gradient bounds and matching traces. If homogeneous notation was intended, clarify it.

findings.historical_status: Confirmed under the usual inhomogeneous W1,2 convention, with an exact local-input counterexample and an explicit repaired construction; visual confirmation pending.

problems.independent_check: Root independently computes the circle-valued harmonic map u_k=(cos(log r/k^2),sin(log r/k^2)) with delta_k=e^-k. Its radial harmonic-map residual vanishes and |grad u_k|^2=1/(k^4 r^2). Every doubling annulus has energy 2 pi log(2)/k^4. For fixed eta the averaged radial length is (k+2 log eta)/k^2, hence the stated iterated limit Lambda is zero. At r=e^(-k/2) the left side of V.3 is k^-4, whereas the claimed RHS/LHS ratio is 4 pi C eta^-beta e^(-beta k/2)(k+2 log(2 eta)) -> 0 for every beta>0 and fixed C,eta.
problems.counterevidence: The actual Lemma V.1 is expressly local on annuli and imposes no global closed-surface extension, full-disk finite energy or extra Hopf constraint. The report explicitly does not apply this map to the stronger Theorem I.2 hypotheses. Even an eventual-in-k reading fails. A finite-stage residual or Lambda+epsilon bound would not be contradicted.
problems.repair_boundary: The example forces a nonzero finite-stage residual despite Lambda=0; k^-4 has log^2-scaled limit zero. The report properly leaves a full corrected general collar estimate unproved.
problems.severity_reason: The uniform quantitative collar lemma is false and is explicitly used at source page 38 toward the main degenerating-domain proof. Major follows from the damaged core derivation; no global index-theorem counterexample is claimed.

problems.independent_check: Root independently verifies psi=(1-|xi|^2)_+^4, phi0=partial_2 psi, b0=-Delta psi and a0=xi1 chi(|xi|^2). The C3/C2/C1 zero extensions introduce no boundary distribution terms, and grad a0=e1 on the support of grad b0, so J(a0,b0)=-Delta phi0. Rescaling about (1-3 epsilon,0) puts all data strictly inside B1 and preserves their Dirichlet energies. The LHS is at least (1-4 epsilon)^2 Ephi, while f(r)=r^2 log^2(1+1/r) log(1+log(1/r)) is at most 32 epsilon on the support. Thus the displayed universal bound fails for sufficiently small epsilon.
problems.exact_calculation_check: Without rerunning code, root independently checks Ephi=1152 pi Beta(3,5)=384 pi/35; Eb=36864 pi integral_0^1 u(1-u)^2(2u-1)^2 du=3072 pi/5 using integral=1/60; and the cutoff substitution u=1+3q gives Ea=184 pi/35. The weight-to-boundary-distance limit is log(2)^2. Retained original script and actual stdout were fully read, and remain original execution.
problems.repair_check: Root checks the dyadic gradient decomposition, including the first outer annulus; zero total compact Jacobian removes the exterior logarithmic harmonic mode, and the inner gap gives harmonic energy decay. With B_j=2^-j ||grad b_j||_2, the weighted estimate separates a geometric convolution and tails T_k. Telescoping gives sum T_k^2 <= 4 sum (k+1)^2 B_k^2 for arbitrary finite nonnegative sequences, and Wente continuity passes to the L2 gradient decomposition. This proves the replacement weight r^2(1+log(1/r))^2. It is positive at one and o(r^alpha) at zero. In downstream geometric summation an exponent alpha' in (max(alpha,log_2(3/2)),2) may be used to avoid the resonant ratio, then the requested weaker decay follows; no finite-sample summation inference is used.
problems.severity_reason: Lemma E.1 is a false core analytic inequality, explicitly invoked at F.7 in the neck-estimate chain. Availability of the verified replacement does not make the printed bound true. The report correctly limits the repair and avoids claiming either main index theorem false.

problems.independent_check: Root differentiates pi(z)=z/|z| and expands pi((1+at,bt)) to second order: acceleration (-b^2,-2ab), whereas D_(b e2)P_e1(a e1+b e2)=(-b^2,-ab). The stated variation is arbitrary ambient phi, so the example meets its assumptions. The actual off-target derivative has factor |z|^-1. Also d(I-u tensor u)=-du tensor u-u tensor du, not the printed antisymmetric tensor combination.
problems.repair_check: The acceleration discrepancy is tangential; the normal acceleration is I(w,w). At a critical point the first-variation contribution of a changed tangential acceleration vanishes, so the Hessian depends only on initial tangent velocity. The source's subsequent contraction and final sphere Hessian are already the correct ones.
problems.severity_reason: The local identities are false, but the second-variation interface is restored and the final Hessian/spectral operator is not refuted; Minor is appropriate.

problems.independent_check: For the intended extension in Lemma C.1, a=1 on 1<|x|<3 satisfies all input assumptions. A gradient-only bound forces its extension to be constant one, which is not in inhomogeneous W1,2(C). The source proof explicitly describes extension of a, so an unrelated zero output is not a repair of that claimed operation. Independently, the printed chi_R is identically one inside B_R and fails to match a general boundary trace.
problems.counterevidence: If W1,2(C) was intended homogeneously, the function-space issue is a clarification; the report expressly states this. The explicit cutoff/boundary-matching problem remains.
problems.repair_check: Use chi_(R/2), the outer function breve a under inversion, and the homogeneous formulation with tilde a-a_R in W1,2(C). Since R/2>r, the construction uses only available values, matches traces, becomes constant outside B_(2R), and scaled annular Poincare plus conformal invariance gives the stated gradient bounds. The inner construction is analogous.
problems.severity_reason: A correct extension required by subsequent gradient/Jacobian arguments is recovered without changing those uses; Minor, with no claimed main-theorem failure.
